request: Our biggest customer contract (attached) has an availability SLA and our VP Engineering wants us to go active-active across two cloud regions next quarter at about $41k/month extra. Her reasoning: we should target 99.99%, which 'still gives us around 52 minutes of downtime a month', and region failure is our biggest risk. I've attached the contract clause, our incident log for the last 12 months and the cost estimate. Should we approve the multi-region project?

expected.summary: The downtime math is wrong: 99.99% over a 30-day month allows only about 4.3 minutes, not 52 (52.6 minutes is the yearly allowance), and the contract actually requires 99.95%, i.e. 21.6 minutes per 30-day month. The incident log shows zero region-wide outages; bad deploys caused 92 of 115 customer-facing minutes (80%), and the two months that exceeded 21.6 minutes (January, 38; August, 22) were both deploy-driven, so active-active would not have prevented most downtime and adds deployment complexity. Key information is also missing: RPO/RTO and the ledger consistency model are TBD. Recommendation: do not approve active-active now; invest first in deploy safety (progressive delivery, automated rollback, migration checks) and certificate automation, define RPO/RTO, and consider a cheaper warm-standby DR option.
